name: Learn basic lip-reading
blurb: Honest expectations: only about a third of speech sounds are visible on the lips, so lip-reading is mostly context and pattern prediction. Even partial skill is useful in noisy rooms.
gear: Videos with subtitles you can toggle
steps: Learn the visemes: the visually distinct mouth shapes. P, B and M look identical; F and V look identical; many sounds are invisible entirely.
Learn to read whole words and phrases rather than sound by sound — context does most of the work.
Practise with subtitled video: watch with subtitles off, guess, then turn them on to check.
Practise with a partner mouthing common phrases from a known set, then from an unknown one.
Learn to use every other cue: facial expression, gesture, topic, and the shape of the conversation.
Practise in real conditions — a noisy café is the actual use case.
tips: Even expert lip-readers rely heavily on guessing from context. Do not judge yourself against a fantasy.
Beards, poor light and people who turn away make it impossible. That is the medium, not you.
proof: You follow the gist of a subtitled conversation with the sound off and subtitles hidden.
